question:
**(Workforce Allocation for Project Management Case Study)**

A consulting firm allocates three teams to three different projects. The initial manpower allocation is given by $M = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 7 & 1 \\ 6 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$, rows are teams, columns are projects.

Each project needs a minimum of $\begin{bmatrix}20 \\ 18 \\ 22\end{bmatrix}$ man-hours.

(a) Form a system of equations and determine if the given allocation meets project requirements uniquely.  
(b) If a unique allocation exists, calculate how much manpower each team must supply to each project by solving the system.  
(c) Discuss critically how altering just one element of $M$ might affect the existence and uniqueness of the allocation.
explanation:
(a)
Let $X = \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3\end{bmatrix}$ = hours supplied by each team.
$MX = B$

(b)
Compute determinant:
$|M| = 4\begin{vmatrix}7 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{vmatrix} - 3\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 6 & 3\end{vmatrix} + 5\begin{vmatrix}2 & 7 \\ 6 & 2\end{vmatrix}$
$= 4(7\times3-1\times2) - 3(2\times3-1\times6) + 5(2\times2-7\times6)$
$= 4(21-2) - 3(6-6) + 5(4-42)$
$= 4(19) - 3(0) + 5(-38)$
$= 76+ 0 - 190 = -114$
Unique solution exists.
Using adjugate, solve $X=M^{-1}B$.
Stepwise computation of all minors, cofactors, adjugate, and product.

(c)
If any single element of $M$ is changed, $|M|$ may become zero or remain nonzero:
- If $|M| = 0$, system loses uniqueness—allocation may not be possible or becomes infinitely possible (if consistent).
- For project managers, careful assignment ensures unique, achievable allocations.

options.A:
(a) $MX=B$, where $M=\begin{bmatrix}4&3&5\\2&7&1\\6&2&3\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}20\\18\\22\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $|M|=0$, the system has no unique solution.
(c) Any change in one element always makes the system inconsistent.
options.B:
(a) $MX=B$, where $M=\begin{bmatrix}4&3&5\\2&7&1\\6&2&3\end{bmatrix}$, $X=\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\\x_3\end{bmatrix}$, and $B=\begin{bmatrix}20\\18\\22\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $|M|=-114\ne0$, a unique solution exists and $X=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{51}{19}\\\frac{32}{19}\\\frac{16}{19}\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) Altering one element may keep the determinant non-zero or make it zero; if it becomes zero, uniqueness is lost.
options.C:
(a) $MX=B$, where $M=\begin{bmatrix}4&3&5\\2&7&1\\6&2&3\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $|M|=114\ne0$, the unique solution is $X=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{16}{19}\\\frac{32}{19}\\\frac{51}{19}\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) Altering one element has no effect on determinant or uniqueness.
options.D:
(a) $MX=B$, where $B=\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\\x_3\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $|M|=-114$, the system is inconsistent.
(c) A non-zero determinant means no allocation is possible.
